questions.solution:
one → ❌ Incorrect. "With one other" would mean only two people, which doesn’t fit the general idea of communication among people.

only → ❌ Incorrect. "With only other" is grammatically wrong and meaningless.

some → ❌ Incorrect. "With some other" could work in certain contexts, but here the passage is about communication in general, not a subset.

each → ✅ Correct. "With each other" is the standard collocation in English to express mutual sharing of information.
